Earlier this year, Apple closed off part of the Apple Park Visitor Center, citing plans to "improve our store."

The space has now reopened, with the biggest change being the removal of Apple's custom iPad-based augmented reality experience for viewing Apple Park.

When the Apple Park Visitor Center opened to the public in 2017, the company promoted the AR experience as follows:

Using augmented reality to bring a 3D model of the campus to life, guests are invited to explore Apple Park in an immersive way. Visitors can learn about the largest naturally ventilated building in the world and view one of the largest on-site solar installations globally. Guests can also choose to lift the entire roof to peek inside at the collaborative working spaces.

Before this change, the Apple Park Visitor Center was split into three areas: the AR exhibit, a traditional-style Apple Store, and a café.

Apple has now decommissioned the AR exhibit and converted the space into an extension of the traditional Apple Store. According to MacRumors, this includes Avenues accessory display walls along the walls and redesigned display tables showcasing Apple products.

The rest of the Apple Park Visitor Center, including the café, remains unchanged.

9to5Mac Opinion

The AR experience at the Apple Park Visitor Center was truly one of a kind, but nine years on, it's starting to feel like the space could be put to better use elsewhere.

I was hoping Apple wouldn't simply turn it into another generic retail store and would try something different instead, but thankfully the café is still around and remains a highlight of the Apple Park Visitor Center.
